title: Preparing to go
tomorrow: Baba's in the hospital now. what do you do at a bedside?

segments.voice: Yesterday, letting go of roles: pass it on, and bow while you do it. Simran has been reading Baba's gutka to him at night. Now he wants his phone.
screen: `PASS IT ON.` → `NOW HE WANTS HIS PHONE.`

segments.voice: Somewhere in your contacts, maybe, is a name you scroll past on purpose. Baba Kartar has one. He asks Simran to find it, because the screen is too small for him: Gurnam. They drove trucks together once, then fell out over money, and that was that, for a very long time. Simran dials and hands it over. It rings and rings. A man's voice answers, older and rougher than she expected. Gurnam, Baba says. It's Kartar. Then nobody says anything at all, and Simran isn't sure whether to leave the room.
screen: `A NAME YOU SCROLL PAST.` → `GURNAM. IT'S KARTAR.` → `THEN, SILENCE.`

segments.voice: Earlier that week Baba had asked Harjit for a folder: his papers, his wishes, one page that says keep it simple. Plans are part of getting ready. But the Sikh picture of getting ready is bigger than a folder. Kirtan Sohila, the prayer before sleep, opens on a wedding. Guru Nanak writes, on Ang 12, in paraphrase: the day of the wedding is already written; come, friends, pour oil on the threshold, and give me your blessing to meet my Lord. The soul is the bride, death is the day she goes to meet her groom, and her friends gather to get her ready. Here's the thing to tell someone tonight: the Sikh bedtime prayer begins on a wedding day, and the wedding is the soul's going home. Getting ready means papers, and it also means people. Kabir, whose verses are in the Granth, puts it plainly, on Ang 1372, in paraphrase: where there is forgiveness, God himself is there. On the phone, Gurnam finally speaks. Kartar, you fool, he says. What took you so long? Both of them are laughing, and one of them is crying.
screen: `A FOLDER: KEEP IT SIMPLE.` · `THE WEDDING DAY IS WRITTEN.` · `FRIENDS POUR OIL AT THE DOOR.` · `WHERE FORGIVENESS IS, GOD IS.` · then, large: `MAKE PEACE.`

segments.voice: Think of one person where something is unfinished between you: a small hurt, a silence that went on too long. While the sit runs, write the first line of a message to them. Send it if it feels right, or save it as a draft; one honest line is a start.
Preparing to go. In Kirtan Sohila the last day is a wedding day; getting ready means plans, and peace made while there's time.
For the rest of today: make peace, one line at a time, before it's a folder. Done for now.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila before sleep each night, and it is also sung at the end of a life; families facing an elder's last season make practical plans and try to settle old quarrels.

myth: in Kirtan Sohila, death is pictured as a wedding day

fork.reveal: Kabir: where forgiveness is, God is. Baba Kartar didn't wait for a funeral; he made the call while there was time.
